text:
matt-h: incident-bot alerted ~03:12 UTC — spike in 5xx and DNS timeouts from eu customers hitting Private (europe-west3)

incident-bot: [ALERT] service: inference-api, metric: upstream_5xx_rate, threshold: 5% -> 8.7% (eu-region) :bangbang:

matt-h: paging @oncall-azure and tagging @lee-net — looks like a DNS resolution error for our private model-resolver within europe-west3 VPC peering paths. customers on Private reported model load failures + retries.

jules: got the page, joining. initial checks: control plane OK, host-level health checks green, but resolver logs show lots of SERVFAIL and truncated responses.

lee-net: seeing increased NXDOMAIN/SERVFAIL from the region's managed DNS (gcloud-dns) toward our on-prem forwarders. Also some asymmetric responses — queries going to eu-west3 but returning answers with eu-west1 IPs.

alex-ml: user impact: model-init failures cause 502s from the customer-facing gateway; embeddings endpoints falling back to hosted models for some tenants. noisy but limited to Private deployments routed through that region.

matt-h: collecting quick evidence — paste of dig from one of affected nodes:

```
$ dig +short @169.254.169.253 resolver.internal.redwood model-eu-west3.internal
;; connection timed out; no servers could be reached
$ dig +noall +comment +stats model-eu-west3.internal
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: SERVFAIL, id: 12345
;; flags: qr rd ra; QUERY: 1, ANSWER: 0, AUTHORITY: 1, ADDITIONAL: 1
```

jules: routing table snapshots show a flurry of BGP withdraws from a GCP POP in europe-west3 at ~03:10 UTC, which line up with when the DNS start failing.

lee-net: contacting GCP support now (SR# 024123-GBG). provisional note: "investigating DNS resolvers returning stale records due to downstream peering instability". ETA unknown.

oncall-azure: acknowledged, standing by for escalation. can we mitigate at the platform layer?

matt-h: yes — immediate mitigations we can attempt: 1) increase local DNS cache TTL on platform resolvers to reduce repeat queries, 2) temporarily route Private EU traffic to europe-west2 as a fallback for new model loads (smart routing), 3) enable a conservative host-level retry/backoff to reduce amplification.

alex-ml: fallback routing will require a model compatibility check — europe-west2 hosts a compatible model variant (v1.2) for most workloads, should be fine for a temporary redirect.

jules: doing the on-call handoff to @lee-net for network troubleshooting and to @alex-ml for model routing. matt — can you draft an external customer note for impacted clusters? @alice-csm should get looped in.

matt-h: drafting short customer-facing blurb (for CSMs and Status):

"We are investigating increased DNS resolution failures in GCP europe-west3 that are affecting Private deployments. Some model loads may fail or experience increased latency. We have put temporary mitigations in place (DNS caching and rerouting) and will update within 30 minutes. No data loss."

alice-csm: thanks — I'll start notifying the small set of impacted enterprise customers and include the mitigation steps and expected behavior (models may load from fallback region).

lee-net: pushing cache-ttl change to platform resolvers now (increase from 30s -> 300s) and enabling conditional stub routing to europe-west2 for requests that fail resolution locally. Rolling config with canary.

ops-bot: deploy started: resolver-ttl-bump v2 -> canary (hosts: resolver-canary-{1,2}), rollout id 88421

jules: while cache TTL warms, I'll monitor for truncated/edns issues — truncated responses hint at MTU/path issues causing UDP fallbacks to TCP which can time out.

matt-h: good point — any logs showing "truncated"?

lee-net: yes, captured in resolver logs at 03:11:45:

```
[03:11:45] resolver.go:421 WARN truncated response from 34.72.12.10 (gcp-dns-pop)
[03:11:45] resolver.go:430 WARN retrying over TCP
[03:11:47] resolver.go:447 ERROR tcp handshake timeout
```

alex-ml: given the TCP fallback timeouts, the added cache will stop repeated retries, and routing to europe-west2 avoids the bad POP entirely. initiating a traffic policy update now.

matt-h: note to oncall: temporarily widen smart-routing policy for private-eu -> prefer europe-west2 for model-resolver requests for 45m. Patch id: policy-2026-03-15-01

ops-bot: policy update applied to 60% of nodes (rolling): policy-2026-03-15-01

jules: GCP just responded on the SR: "We observed transient packet loss between POPs in europe-west3 causing DNS UDP truncation, engineering is applying a mitigation. We'll update in 30m."

alice-csm: customers acknowledge workaround ok, one asked if IP allowlist changes required — letting them know no changes needed on their side, traffic still originates/terminates within Redwood network.

lee-net: monitoring shows 70% drop in DNS errors after TTL bump + routing. 5xx rate down from 8.7% -> 2.1% in 12m.

matt-h: great. plan for next 60m: keep policy in place, monitor for regressions, coordinate with GCP for final fix. prepare a short post-incident summary after closure.

jules: handing incident to morning shift (handoff note): ongoing — DNS instability in europe-west3 causing SERVFAIL/502s for Private model loads; temporary mitigations: resolver TTL increased, smart-routing to europe-west2, on-call watching; GCP investigating popup-level packet loss. contact SR# 024123-GBG.

lee-net: filing internal follow-up action items:
- run traceroutes from each POP to identify MTU/fragmentation candidates
- add TCP dial timeout tuning for resolver client
- add per-region automatic fallback policy for Private model-resolver

alex-ml: I'll add an eval to ensure model variant parity across fallback regions and monitor quality regressions for the next 72h.

matt-h: closing loop to customers in 1h with update. if GCP confirms fix, we'll plan to revert smart-routing after 30m of normal metrics.

incident-bot: incident resolved (monitoring) — 03:56 UTC. Summary: platform mitigations + GCP network fix reduced error rate to baseline.

matt-h: thanks team. will write a short postmortem draft and tag owners for follow-ups. :thumbsup:
